title: Private Deploy CI/CD Safety Net & Operator Notes
body:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for private (VPC / on‑prem) CI/CD and release mechanics focused on creating operator safety nets: automated checks, signing and attestation integration, upgrade plans with clear rollback windows, and Terraform module expectations for infra changes.

Scope and intent:
- Applies to: Private control plane + on‑prem node pools + cluster-local services (redwood-runtime, sidecars, routing)
- Primary goal: allow safe push of Helm upgrades via GitOps (Argo) while guaranteeing a clear automated rollback path if regressions or infra drift occur.

High level pipeline (recommended pattern)
1) Build: container build in CI (kaniko/buildkit) -> produce semver+buildmeta tag (e.g. v2.3.1+20251103.shaabcd)
2) Test: unit, integration tests; local k8s smoke tests in ephemeral cluster
3) SBOM & signing: generate SBOM (syft), sign image and SBOM with cosign using KMS‑backed key (see signing section)
4) Publish: push image to customer registry (or staging registries) and create image promotion metadata in the registry repo
5) GitOps: create PR to repo managed by Argo (app-of-apps) that points to the new Helm chart/image tag
6) Preflight: automated preflight job (Terraform plan + kube preflight) validates cluster resources & chart values
7) Canary: Argo Rollouts/Helm chart configured for canary weights with automatic analysis hooks
8) Promote/Rollback: either promote to stable tag after analysis passes, or trigger automated rollback on SLO breach or failed checks

Preflight checklist (must pass before merge into main gitops branch)
- Terraform plan for infra changes exists and reviewed (no destructive nodepool replacements without signoff)
- Helm value schema validation (helm template + kubeval) passes for target cluster version
- Images referenced are signed and SBOM attached to the image metadata
- Required KMS keys/secrets present in target cluster (kms: key-id annotation in namespace)
- Nightly canary window reserved in calendar if the release touches critical networking or storage components
- Run quick smoke tests against a canary namespace: readiness, liveness, basic inference path, auth flows

Image signing & attestation (recommended minimal configuration)
- Tooling: cosign (sigstore), syft for SBOM, in-toto attestation for provenance
- Key storage: Use cloud KMS or HSM for cosign key material. For air-gapped customers, store signing keys in customer HSM and provide verification public key to Redwood during onboarding.
- Signing flow in CI:
  - syft -o json <image> > image.sbom.json
  - cosign sign --key k8s://projects/.../locations/.../keyRings/.../cryptoKeys/... <image>
  - cosign attest --predicate image.sbom.json --key k8s://... <image>
- Registry metadata policy: require image signature + sbom attestation for promotion to the "promoted" image tag (handled by CI gate)
- Verification at deploy time: Argo pre-sync hook runs cosign verify for the reference image; fail sync if verification fails

Terraform module notes (infra changes that commonly appear alongside upgrades)
- Modules should be small and composable: network, storage, k8s-cluster, node-pool, monitoring
- Module interface conventions:
  - inputs: name_prefix, environment, tags (list), secure_boot (bool), maintenance_window (string)
  - outputs: resource_ids (list), kubeconfig_secret_name (string)
- State & drift expectations:
  - Use remote state with locking (backend: s3/azure/gcs) and enforce state locking in CI
  - Before applying, run plan and a plan-parser job to produce human-readable summary and risk tags (e.g., "unsafe_replacement: true")
- Safe upgrade guidance:
  - Node pool replacements must be explicit; prefer in-place upgrades where supported
  - For changes that recreate nodes, require a maintenance approval and run cluster-level soak tests post-apply

Helm chart & values conventions
- Charts should be declarative and idempotent; avoid imperative lifecycle hooks that mutate external infra
- Values schema: include a top-level "release" section with fields: version, promote (bool), canary (object), probes (object)
- Canary config example:
  - release.canary.enabled = true
  - release.canary.steps = [ {duration: "5m", weight: 10}, {duration: "15m", weight: 50} ]
- Sidecar/compat checks: charts must include a compatibility matrix for sidecar versions and apiVersion of CRDs used

Argo/GitOps mechanics and operator safety nets
- App structure: use app-of-apps pattern where customer environment repo points to a single app manifest for redwood stack. This makes rollbacks localized to app manifests instead of global trees.
- Sync hooks:
  - pre-sync: cosign verify + terraform-plan-checker (no resource replacements flagged)
  - sync: helm upgrade --install equivalent managed by Argo
  - post-sync: smoke tests + prometheus metric check
- Automated analysis: use Argo Rollouts analysis provider (Prometheus) to track errors, request latency (p50/p95), and tokenized cost-per-1k-requests
- Automatic rollback triggers:
  - >1% error rate increase sustained for 5 minutes
  - p95 latency increase > 2x baseline for 10 minutes
  - health probe failures on >10% pods in a deployment
- Manual gates: designate a release owner to approve promotion to stable after canary finishes; require explicit PR merge + label `promote/stable`

Rollback and emergency flows
- Fast rollback path (automated): Argo Rollouts reverts weights to previous stable images if analysis fails
- Operator-initiated rollback steps:
  1) Identify failing app via alerts/dashboards
  2) Open a short-lifecycle incident branch in gitops repo and revert app manifest to previous image tag
  3) Push and let Argo sync the revert; watch post-sync hooks
  4) Recreate missing resources if the revert removed a required CRD (run post-rollback hook to reapply CRD)
- Timeouts and expectations:
  - Aim to complete rollback of user-facing path within 15 minutes in most cases; communicate expected window in customer-facing incident notes
  - If rollback involves infra-level replacements (node pools), expect longer windows (hours) and trigger on-call escalation

Smoke tests and canary validation (must be runnable in CI and as Argo hooks)
- Tests to run:
  - health endpoint check (200 + body sanity)
  - inference pipeline happy path (small prompt/expected hint)
  - auth/identity roundtrip (token issuance and acceptance)
  - storage persistence check for write-read
- Test harness should be parametric so we can point at canary namespace and run same tests as CI. Failures should produce structured JSON failures so Argo analysis can pick them up.

Observability and SLOs used for rollbacks
- Minimum metrics to track:
  - request_error_rate, request_latency_p95, pod_restart_count, cpu_steal, mem_pressure
  - infra metrics: node_cpu_saturation, kube_api_5xx
- Traces: sample 1% of requests for full tracing, include request token/route metadata for correlating to cost
- Dashboards: per-cluster release dashboard showing baseline vs canary overlays, top 5 endpoints by error delta

Operator-runbook snippets (cheat sheet)
- Verify image signature manually:
  - cosign verify --key <public-key-file> <image>
- Quick revert to previous image tag in gitops:
  - git checkout -b incident/revert-<app>-<ts>
  - sed -i 's:tag: v2.3.1:tag: v2.3.0:' overlays/<cluster>/<app>/values.yaml
  - git commit -am "revert <app> to v2.3.0 due to increased p95"
  - git push origin incident/revert-<app>-<ts> and open a PR to main with label incident/revert
- Force a sync after PR merge (Argo CLI): argocd app sync <app> --prune --timeout 300s

Terraform plan gating in CI (example annotations)
- On PR: run terraform plan and annotate PR with table:
  - changed_resources: 4
  - replacements: 1 (node_pool.foo)
  - risk_tag: recreate-nodepool
- Gating rule: block merge when risk_tag contains recreate-nodepool unless label `infra:allow-recreate` present

Security/Key rotation notes
- Rotate signing keys annually; provide a key rotation plan to customer. Steps:
  1) Create new key in KMS
  2) Update CI to sign with new key (dual-sign during transition period)
  3) Update Argo pre-sync verification keys
  4) Revoke old key after 7 days of successful deployments in the wild
- For air-gapped installs, establish an offline signing protocol and a verification policy that uses a stored public key bundle delivered via administrative channel

Known open questions (action items)
- How to enforce SBOM retention policy in private registries: retention vs storage cost (Priya to prototype indexer)
- Policy for auto-approving infra changes that don't alter node replacements: what thresholds are acceptable? (product + infra engineering decision)
- Should we provide a lightweight operator that performs local cosign verification in place of pre-sync hook for high-latency control planes? (SRE/Runtime to evaluate)

Appendix: sample CI pipeline stages (concise)
- build
- unit-test
- integration-test
- sbom-generate
- sign-image
- push-to-registry
- register-promotion-candidate (write metadata to registry-index)
- pr-to-gitops (create branch/PR)
- preflight (terraform-plan-check + helm-template + cosign-verify)
- schedule-canary (label PR with canary/auto-merge when ok)

Next steps for this doc:
- Convert high-priority items into tickets (see linked artifacts) and prototype a cosign pre-sync Argo hook container image
- Run a tabletop incident rehearsal with a simulated canary failure and measure rollback end-to-end time

Notes to self:
- Keep the playbook lean; avoid adding cluster-specific assumptions. Make hooks small and idempotent so customers can opt into them.
